findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so no absolute affinity benefit can be read from these observations.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.00-0.49 within the declared learning window [0.0,0.5], with curve support reported as [0.0,0.49]; continuous contrast functions are evaluated only at observed nodes with extrapolation disallowed.

Continuous landmark contrast features show large first-to-last rate reversals with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z -72.4 to last_rate_z +5.5 with 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dxy first_rate_z +64.8 to last_rate_z -19.7 with 9 sign changes and 14 strong conflicts), so a constant-rate rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule would be unstable.

Whole-window z values for these landmark features are small in magnitude (e.g. -0.30, +0.10, -0.02, -0.58) and polynomial fits are not accepted, so the observed contrasts do not establish a stable signed direction at the selection nodes.

These continuous features are predicted-endpoint world-coordinate descriptors (soft mass and local displacement/covariance components), i.e. geometric coordinate contrasts, not physical interaction energies and not evidence of neural-module causation.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned coordinate contrast at observed score nodes
hypotheses.falsifier: A validated fit with accepted polynomial and no strong sign conflicts across independent batches would weaken this limitation; its absence keeps the hypothesis descriptive.
hypotheses.observable: landmark local displacement/covariance contrast evaluated at observed score times
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned landmark coordinate contrast could in principle track the observed-node sign reversals, but the supplied evidence does not support committing to one because fits are rejected, sign changes are frequent and strong sign conflicts are present.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or outcome evaluation data are supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Selection enrichment versus absolute geometric descriptor cannot be separated from the read rows alone.
Independent-batch agreement, multiplicity-adjusted support and coverage tables were not read in this turn, so uncertainty-ranked coordinate priorities are not established.
No supported registered coordinate intervention is identified from the evidence read; the finding remains descriptive.
